title: POC scoping - data handling (Aurora Health)
customer_attendees: Dr. Lisa Chen (Director of Data Science)
summary: Discovery/POC scoping for a HIPAA-adjacent POC. Customer needs clarity on PII redaction, log retention, prompt storage, and whether hosted/dedicated/private options meet regulatory needs. Agreed on benchmark targets, sample dataset preparation, and next steps to exchange security docs and run a 48–72 hour load/latency benchmark in Redwood Dedicated trial.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-12-18 15:00 PST (52m)
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Elena Morales (Redwood SE), Dr. Lisa Chen (Aurora Data Science), Marco Alvarez (Aurora Security), Priya Singh (Aurora PM)
---
00:00 - Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, I'm Samir, AE on the account, and Elena our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
00:08 - Lisa: Good, thanks. we'll jump in, we have a bunch of questions around data handling for the POC, mostly PII and logs.
00:14 - Elena: Great, that's exactly what we wanted to cover — we'll walk through options (hosted, dedicated, private) and how data is stored, retention, redaction, and baseline benchmark targets.
01:02 - Marco: quick context: Aurora is a healthcare SaaS, some data is PHI-ish, we are not yet signed to a full BAA but that might be needed depending on the POC. for now we want to see what redaction and data controls Redwood offers.
01:22 - Samir: Yep understood. To frame the POC — what success looks like for you? latency, cost, and zero data leakage are usually the trifecta.
01:35 - Priya: Success criteria: 1) accuracy on our clinical-note summarization (ROUGE-ish metrics) 2) p50 latency under 200ms and p95 under 600ms for our typical payloads, 3) no raw PHI stored in logs or prompt archives, and 4) ability to run a 48–72 hour throughput test with ~10 concurrent users.
02:03 - Elena: Good specifics. for workload sizing can you share typical token lengths and QPS?
02:12 - Lisa: Typical request is 700–1200 tokens including context and prompt, average user concurrency during POC expected 8–12, QPS around 3–5 sustained, bursts to 15.
02:30 - Elena: ok that maps to a mid-sequence load, we will recommend a 2-GPU Dedicated pilot for the target model to meet p95 SLA while keeping cost reasonable for the POC.
03:00 - Marco: storage question — do you keep prompts or user messages after the request? we need to know default retention and whether that can be disabled for our org.
03:14 - Samir: By default Redwood stores request/response logs for 30 days for debugging and analytics, but for Dedicated/Private you can opt out or shorten retention. we also support redaction pipelines that remove PII before storing.
03:29 - Marco: redaction pipelines — is that automatic or do we have to provide regexes? how reliable is it for PHI?
03:37 - Elena: we have a couple approaches: client-side redaction (recommended), server-side redaction with customizable rules, and a policy-based filter that tags PII using a NER model. server-side NER is high-recall but not perfect — we recommend client-side tokenization/PHI hashing for strict compliance.
04:05 - Lisa: ok so for the POC we should send a sanitized sample set and also plan a client-side redaction flow.
04:14 - Priya: related: prompt storage — do you keep the raw prompt by default when feature flags for logging are off?
04:22 - Samir: there's an audit log and a prompt archive feature. if logging is off, prompts are not archived. however certain telemetry like request id, timing, and model version is retained for operational reasons. we can turn off prompt archiving entirely for a Dedicated pilot.
04:44 - Marco: KMS question: can we bring our own keys? we need keys for encryption at rest and HSM for some ops.
04:52 - Elena: yes, we support customer-managed KMS in Dedicated and Private — you can integrate with AWS KMS or an HSM. hosted plans don't support BYOK today.
05:10 - Lisa: HIPAA/BAA — do you have an existing BAA and SOC2?
05:16 - Samir: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II; we can share the report under NDA. for HIPAA we have a BAA offering as part of enterprise/private contracts — we'll route that to legal.
05:30 - Marco: how about audit logs for model access and prompt deletes? we need immutable logs for audits.
05:36 - Elena: Audit logs are available in Dedicated and Private; they capture user actions, model calls, and admin changes. immutable export to your SIEM/S3 is supported.
06:05 - Priya: retention policy granularity? can we set different retention for prompts vs traces vs metrics?
06:12 - Samir: yes. retention can be configured separately: prompts, line-level logs, aggregated metrics. typical POC we set prompts to 0–7 days and metrics longer for cost analysis.
06:30 - Lisa: for the benchmark itself — what metrics will you collect and how will you run it?
06:36 - Elena: we'll run a load harness against the model variant you pick. we'll collect p50/p90/p95 latency, token throughput, GPU util, and tail memory usage. we'll also run quality tests on a held-out sample to track regressions.
07:05 - Samir: timeline — recommendation: week 0 sign-off on scope and security docs, week 1 environment setup and sample data exchange, week 2 run benchmark and tuning, week 3 review results and decision. is that aligned?
07:22 - Priya: that seems fine — our internal stakeholders want results by end of next month.
07:30 - Marco: small thing: can you guarantee no prompts ever show up in backups or S3 buckets you control?
07:36 - Elena: for Dedicated we can configure zero prompt archiving and ensure backups exclude prompt archives. for hosted there's more limitation.
08:00 - Lisa: any chance of model hallucination leaking proprietary data? we want to ensure we don't end up with secret info in generated completions.
08:10 - Elena: model leakage is rare but possible. mitigation: prompt-scoped context removal, strict input redaction, and rate-limits on generation that reference protected identifiers. we can also run adversarial tests as part of the POC.
09:02 - Samir: pricing for a Dedicated short pilot — rough ballpark while still in scoping?
09:10 - Elena: for a 2-GPU Dedicated pilot with reserved capacity for 3–4 weeks plus engineering support, we'll provide a pilot quote — I'll follow up.
09:34 - Priya: benchmarks: can you support our target model (open-model X, 30B)?
09:40 - Elena: yes we have support for the 30B quantized variant; performance characteristics will differ but we can run a configuration that meets your latency targets with the 2-GPU setup.
10:12 - Marco: about logs again — can you provide a way to redact logs after capture, not just prevent capture?
10:20 - Elena: yes, you can run a post-ingest redaction job that redact phrases or hashed identifiers and also run a delete path; but note delete in distributed caches may be eventually consistent. we'll document the deletion guarantees.
11:00 - Lisa: compliance group will want to review retention and deletion SLAs before sign-off.
11:08 - Samir: understood — we'll provide detailed docs and an SLA appendix for the POC.
11:20 - Priya: can we do sample calls to verify that prompts aren't retained? maybe a short live demo?
11:26 - Samir: yes, we can demo turning off prompt archiving and show logs. we'll mask any real PHI during demo.
12:00 - Elena: one more tech note — for latency we recommend enabling KV cache and prefix caching; that typically reduces token generation latency for repeated context. we can tune for your sequence lengths.
12:32 - Marco: are there any known edge cases where KV cache leaks previous prompt data?
12:40 - Elena: KV cache holds internal key-value state for the model, it's per-request session and not durable across unrelated sessions. for strict isolation we recommend session-level encryption and periodic KV flushes between sessions.
13:05 - Lisa: who will run the benchmark on your side — redwood will run it or aurora?
13:12 - Samir: we can run it collaboratively. Redwood will spin the load harness, but we ask Aurora to provide sanitized sample traffic and approve the test plan.
13:34 - Priya: are telemetry exports supported to our DataDog/Splunk?
13:40 - Elena: yes, metrics and traces can be exported via OTLP or direct integration.
14:00 - Samir: ok let's talk concrete next steps — we'll send a package with SOC2, sample SOW, pilot pricing, and a short how-to for client-side redaction.
14:12 - Marco: and we'll prepare a sanitized dataset and an inventory of fields considered PHI.
14:20 - Lisa: timeline again — if we get docs this week we can start environment setup next week.
14:30 - Samir: perfect. any other blockers?
14:36 - Priya: one ask — can Redwood do in-POD redaction pre-model so the model never sees raw PHI?
14:44 - Elena: yes, you can implement that in a pre-processing lambda or sidecar; Redwood also provides hooks for pre-model webhooks for transformations. For Dedicated/Private we can even run your redaction service inside the VPC so raw text never leaves your network.
15:10 - Marco: excellent. a few follow-up questions we'll send in chat about BAA wording.
15:18 - Samir: great. recap?
15:22 - Samir: recap: Redwood to send SOC2 report and security whitepaper, pilot quote for 2-GPU Dedicated, sample SOW, and instructions for client-side redaction. Aurora to provide sanitized sample dataset, PHI inventory, and internal stakeholders for review. schedule benchmark in week 2.
15:48 - Lisa: that works. thanks.
52:00 - (call end)
---
